c.tagline: Northern gateway on the Nan River, home to Thailand's most revered Buddha.

taxi.fareNote: There are few metered street taxis; getting around means flagging a shared songthaew truck or a tuk-tuk and agreeing the short-hop fare (roughly 15-40 baht per person) before you ride, or booking a Grab car. Cycle samlors still ferry passengers short distances near the market.

emergency.note: Tourist Police 1155 has English-speaking operators; 191 reaches police and 1669 the ambulance/medical service.

hood_landmark.Nai Mueang (City Center / Riverside): Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat Phitsanulok
hood_landmark.Wat Chan: Wat Chan Tawantok Nan River Phitsanulok
hood_landmark.Aranyik: Sergeant Major Thawee Folk Museum Phitsanulok

hood_desc: The compact heart of Phitsanulok along the east bank of the Nan River, home to the revered Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai) and its Phra Buddha Chinnarat image, the riverside night bazaar, and most of the city's hotels; best for first-timers who want everything walkable.
The west-bank district across the Nan River, a quieter, mostly residential and local-market area with floating riverside restaurants and easy access back over the bridges to the center.

A northern district known for the Sergeant Major Thawee Folk Museum and the Buranathai Buddha Image Foundry, where the famous Chinnarat replicas are cast; more spread-out, local and craft-focused in feel.
The eastern university quarter around Naresuan University, with student cafes, cheap eateries and a youthful, budget-friendly atmosphere away from the tourist core.
A southern residential and academic fringe near Naresuan University's health-sciences campus and Bueng Phra lake, quiet and green with budget guesthouses.
lodging: The Imperial Hotel & Convention Centre Phitsanulok

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not reliably potable.

transit.pay: Pay songthaews and tuk-tuks in cash directly to the driver — around 15-30 baht per person for short hops in town, agreed before you ride; there is no rechargeable transit card system.
transit.hours: Songthaews, tuk-tuks and cycle samlors run through the day and into the evening, thinning out at night when Grab fills the gap.
transit.note: Phitsanulok has no metro, tram, or urban rail transit; getting around the compact center means songthaew shared trucks, a few local bus routes, tuk-tuks and ride-hailing via Grab, with the classic three-wheeled samlor still working the streets near the market.

bus: Phitsanulok Bus Terminal 2 (intercity coaches to Bangkok, Chiang Mai and Sukhothai)

car.idp: Required (International Driving Permit needed alongside your home license)

train: Phitsanulok Railway Station (State Railway of Thailand northern line, Bangkok–Chiang Mai via Ayutthaya)

transit.m: Airport taxi or Grab to the city center (10-15 min)
Free or low-cost shuttle offered by some central hotels

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up the bill or leaving 20-40 baht for good service at restaurants is appreciated but not required.

food.name: Kuay Teow Hoi Kha
food.desc: Phitsanulok's signature pork noodle soup, eaten at riverside stalls where you sit on a raised bench with your legs dangling over the Nan River.

places.name: Kuay Teow Hoi Kha stalls at Wat Chan Tai
places.note: The original dangling-legs noodle strip; cheap bowls with crisp pork and a river breeze, busy from mid-morning.

places.name: Phitsanulok Night Bazaar
places.note: Several hoi kha vendors set up along the river wall after dark, so you can compare broths in one stroll.

places.name: Talat Sai Market food stalls
places.note: Morning market version favoured by locals, with clear pork broth and homemade fish balls.

food.name: Phak Bung Loi Fa (Flying Vegetable)
food.desc: Morning glory stir-fried with garlic, chilli and fermented bean sauce, then flung flaming through the air to a waiter who catches it on a plate.

places.name: Phitsanulok Night Bazaar riverside restaurants
places.note: The dish was invented here; several open-air kitchens still perform the toss nightly for diners.

places.name: Rim Nan riverside restaurants
places.note: Sit-down riverside spots that pair the flying greens with full Thai menus rather than just the show.

places.name: Wat Yai night food strip
places.area: Near Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat
places.note: Handy after visiting the Phra Buddha Chinnarat temple; smaller crowds than the main bazaar.

food.name: Pla Phao Klua (salt-crusted grilled river fish)
food.desc: Whole Nan River fish packed in salt and lemongrass, grilled over charcoal and eaten with a fiery seafood dipping sauce and fresh herbs.

places.name: Rim Nan riverside restaurants
places.note: Grill stations face the water; ask for pla nin or pla thapthim caught locally.

places.name: Phitsanulok Night Bazaar
places.note: Rows of charcoal grills with fish on display, priced by weight and cooked to order.

places.name: Talat Sai Market
places.note: Daytime grill vendors sell fish to take away, a cheap way to try it before dinner prices.

food.name: Khao Kha Moo
food.desc: Pork leg slow-braised in soy, star anise and cinnamon until it collapses, ladled over rice with pickled mustard greens and a boiled egg.

places.name: Phitsanulok Night Bazaar
places.note: Late-night carts with big steaming pots; the standard cheap supper for locals here.

places.name: Talat Sai Market
places.note: Long-running stalls that sell out by early afternoon, a good sign of turnover.

places.name: Phitsanulok Railway Station night stalls
places.note: Open very late for train arrivals, with generous portions and fast service.

food.name: Kluay Tak (sun-dried bananas)
food.desc: The province's famous sweet: bananas from Bang Krathum flattened and sun-dried until chewy and caramel-toned, sometimes simmered in coconut syrup.

places.name: Talat Sai Market
places.note: The main place to buy fresh batches by weight rather than pre-packed supermarket versions.

places.name: Phitsanulok Night Bazaar
places.note: Souvenir stalls sell honey-glazed and syrup-simmered versions alongside other local sweets.

places.name: Roadside stalls on the Bang Krathum road
places.note: Producer stalls in the growing area itself, the cheapest and freshest source.

food.name: Cha Yen (Thai iced tea)
food.desc: Strong orange-hued tea sweetened with condensed and evaporated milk over crushed ice, the standard cooler with noodles or grilled fish.

places.name: Talat Sai Market drink stalls
places.note: Made to order in the old style with a cloth strainer, and priced for locals.

places.name: Phitsanulok Night Bazaar
places.note: Dozens of drink carts along the riverfront, easy to grab while browsing food stalls.

places.name: Rai Ruen Rom
places.note: Farm cafe on the city outskirts serving iced teas and coffees in a garden setting.

food.name: Oliang (Thai iced black coffee)
food.desc: Dark roasted coffee blended with corn and sesame, brewed strong, sweetened with palm sugar and poured over ice with no milk.

places.name: Talat Sai Market coffee stalls
places.note: Old-school sock-filter brewers running since dawn, the local morning ritual.

places.name: Phitsanulok Railway Station kiosks
places.note: Reliable early and late, and cheap; a Thai travel staple served in a bag with a straw.

places.name: Rai Ruen Rom
places.note: Modern cafe take on oliang using local beans, with seating and air conditioning.

landmarks: Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai)
Home of Phra Buddha Chinnarat, widely hailed as Thailand's most beautiful Buddha image, its flame-haloed gold figure drawing pilgrims from across the kingdom.
Wat Ratchaburana
A venerable riverside temple that survived the 1957 fire that razed old Phitsanulok, cherished for its weathered chedi, murals and giant reclining Buddha.
King Naresuan Shrine & Chandra Palace Ruins (Wang Chan)
The excavated birthplace palace of Thailand's warrior-king Naresuan the Great, honored by a regal shrine where students and soldiers pay respects.
Sergeant Major Thawee Folk Museum
An award-winning trove of vanishing Thai folk life, from rat traps to birthing rituals, lovingly assembled in traditional teak houses.
Buranathai Buddha Image Foundry
A working foundry opposite the folk museum where visitors watch artisans cast, polish and gild bronze Buddha statues using age-old lost-wax techniques.
Nan Riverfront & Night Bazaar
Phitsanulok's evening gathering place, where houseboat-dotted riverbanks host food stalls famous for theatrical 'flying morning glory' stir-fry tossing.
Wat Chulamanee
The city's oldest temple, several kilometers south, whose superb Khmer-style prang predates Ayutthaya and once welcomed a king into brief monkhood.
Wat Aranyik
Atmospheric brick ruins of a forest monastery from the Sukhothai era, its chedi and moat quietly moldering amid residential lanes east of the river.
Wat Nang Phaya
A revered temple adjoining Wat Yai, famed nationwide as the origin of the prized Phra Nang Phaya amulets unearthed in its grounds.
Thai Bird Garden
A sanctuary of caged and free-flying birds beside the Buranathai Buddha foundry, drawing local families and birdwatchers alike.

train.note: No international trains. Phitsanulok is a busy stop on the northern main line, with trains to Bangkok in about 5-6 hours and Chiang Mai in 6, including overnight sleepers in both directions - it is the usual rail gateway for Sukhothai. The station is central. Book on the SRT D-Ticket site up to 90 days ahead.

bus.note: No international coaches. The bus terminal east of the centre runs frequent services to Sukhothai (about an hour), Bangkok (5-6 hours), Chiang Mai and across the north-east toward Khon Kaen, on Transport Co. (https://www.transport.co.th/) and Win Tour. Book through 12Go (https://12go.asia/).

ferry.note: Phitsanulok sits on the Nan river, which carries only local longtail and dinner boats rather than scheduled services, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Sukhothai Historical Park
half.blurb: The UNESCO-listed ruins of Thailand's first capital — serene 13th-14th-century temples, Buddha images and lotus ponds, about 60 km west and the main reason many travelers base in Phitsanulok.

full.name: Si Satchanalai Historical Park
full.blurb: A quieter sister UNESCO site to Sukhothai with forest-wrapped temples and ancient kilns, about 90 km northwest.

full.name: Phu Hin Rong Kla National Park
full.blurb: Mountain park of rock fields and waterfalls that was once the jungle headquarters of the Communist Party of Thailand, about 2.5 hours northeast.

full.name: Thung Salaeng Luang National Park
full.blurb: Rolling savanna grasslands, waterfalls and wildlife in one of Thailand's largest parks, on the road toward Lom Sak.
